newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan March overseas ship orders fall 34 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan March overseas ship orders fall 34 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Japanese shipbuilders won ship export contracts for 42 vessels in March, or 1.2 million gross registered tonnes (grt), down 34 percent from the same month a year earlier, an industry body said on Thursday.
"It's not like Japanese shipyards fared poorly in March, but it's more like their performance was exceptional a year ago," said an official at the Japan Ship Exporters' Association.
Ship export orders won by Japanese shipbuilders totalled 1.82 million grt in March 1995, a 76 percent increase over the corresponding month in 1994.
March orders comprised 12 freighters, 26 bulk carriers, one very large crude carrier (VLCC), one small crude tanker, one oil product tanker and one chemical tanker.

During the first quarter of 1997, Japan won ship export orders for 83 vessels, or 3.14 million grt, while South Korea, another major shipbuilder, secured overseas contracts for 24 ships totalling 1.67 million grt, the official said.
